Lee Sharks's “Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose” is a satirical ars poetica
Lee Sharks's “Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose” is a satirical ars poetica: a manifesto about how to write, what a writer should believe, and what artistic commitment costs.
It borrows the recognizable form of Jack Kerouac's “Belief & Technique for Modern Prose” but turns that form into an experiment
Its governing idea is that no single doctrine of writing can be trusted—not even the doctrine that rejects all doctrines.

atoms.span: Sharks and Feist take that possibility to its extreme
I would describe Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose as an ars poetica that includes satire
Satire is present, sometimes aggressively, but it is not the governing purpose of the work. The governing purpose is to articulate and test a poetics
Its relation to Ginsberg's Footnote to Howl, the avant-garde manifesto tradition, Horace's Ars Poetica, and Kerouac's poetics is relevant to its identity.
The critical edition identifies this operation as sublation: negation, preservation, and transformation.
